description: Authored update to the 09:00 triage exercise. Deployment observations, owners, capacity and timings are supplied scenario facts, not executed observations, scanner output or a real incident. Threat data is the same dated snapshot as the 09:00 packet; no newer EPSS or KEV data was consulted.
capacity: Two engineers are free from 13:00 to 17:00 besides the service owners. Owners: Mira (ledger-admin), Jon (document-files), Lea (legacy-preview), Sam (report-renderer).

items.evidence: Ingress audit 12:40: the administrative ingress allows the corporate VPN range and the partner support network (41 external support accounts), not only the administrator subnet recorded at 09:00. Packaging unchanged: the same executable Spring Boot JAR on JDK 17. The prepared upgrade to a supported Spring Framework release passed unit tests; the integration environment is booked for 16:00 today.

Containment 10:05: the static file route was disabled by configuration. Verification 10:20: the traversal request now returns 404, and so do intended document downloads for the Birch Legal portal, which used the same route; 14 support tickets so far. Upgrade build passes; one integration test fails on resource caching headers. The product owner asks to re-enable the route until the upgrade ships. The application still runs on Reactor Netty without the Spring Security HTTP Firewall.

Deployed artifact retrieved 09:52: a WAR on Apache Tomcat, JDK 11, spring-webmvc 5.3.17; the artifact identity differs from the inventory record used at 09:00. Public endpoint confirmed. The public-access restriction requested at 10:00 has not been applied: it needs the edge team, available from 14:00.

New scanner match 12:15. A route listing captured from the deployed instance at 12:45 shows annotated @RestController endpoints only and no RouterFunctions resource handlers; static assets are served by the CDN. Internal service with no internet ingress; runs on Reactor Netty.
